title: Simultaneous spreading of a closed generic cover and dense complements
statement:
Let $f:X	o Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $I$ be a finite index set, and for each $i\in I$ let $j_i:Z_i\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that $h_i=f\circ j_i$ is of finite type. Write $D_i=j_i(Z_i)$ and $D_{i,t}=p_t^{-1}(D_i)\subseteq X_t$, where $X_t$ is the ordinary scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $p_t:X_t	o X$ is its canonical projection. Suppose the closed subsets $C_i=D_{i,\eta}$ are nonempty and irreducible, cover $X_\eta$, and satisfy $C_i
ot\subseteq C_j$ whenever $i
e j$. Then there is an open subset $V\subseteq Y$ containing $\eta$ such that, for every $t\in V$, the closed subsets $D_{i,t}$ are all nonempty, satisfy $X_t= igcup_{i\in I}D_{i,t}$, and for every $i
e j$ the relatively open subset $D_{i,t}\setminus D_{j,t}$ is dense in $D_{i,t}$. Here dense means that its closure in the subspace $D_{i,t}$ is all of $D_{i,t}$. No irreducibility of a specialized piece $D_{i,t}$ is asserted. Empty $I$ is allowed; the covering hypothesis then means $X_\eta=\varnothing$. No Noetherianity, separatedness, flatness, or reducedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0554 (lemma-irreducible-components-in-neighbourhood), proof: from the pairwise intersections $Z_{i,j}$ through the successive shrinkings and the open neighbourhood contained in every $f(X_i)$; returned Steps 4--6 and the base-open intersection in Step 7

proof.text: Write $q_{i,t}:(Z_i)_t\to Z_i$ for the fibre projection of $h_i$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $j_i$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $D_i$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $q_{i,t}$ and $p_t$ are homeomorphisms onto $h_i^{-1}(\{t\})$ and $f^{-1}(\{t\})$, respectively. The restriction of $j_i$ maps $h_i^{-1}(\{t\})$ homeomorphically onto $D_i\cap f^{-1}(\{t\})$: indeed $h_i(z)=f(j_i(z))$, and every point of $D_i$ has a unique preimage under $j_i$. Composing these restrictions gives a homeomorphism $a_{i,t}:|(Z_i)_t|\longrightarrow D_{i,t}$ characterized by $p_t(a_{i,t}(u))=j_i(q_{i,t}(u))$. The set $D_{i,t}=p_t^{-1}(D_i)$ is closed in $X_t$, since $D_i$ is closed and $p_t$ is continuous. In particular $a_{i,\eta}$ identifies $|(Z_i)_\eta|$ with $C_i$.

source.place: Tag 0554, proof: viewing the closed pieces and their intersections inside each fibre; fibre-topology discussion immediately before Tag 054Y

proof.text:
For $i
e j$, put $W_{ij}=Z_i\setminus j_i^{-1}(D_j)$, an open subset of $Z_i$. Step 1 identifies $q_{i,t}^{-1}(W_{ij})$ with $D_{i,t}\setminus D_{j,t}$: for $u\in|(Z_i)_t|$, the defining equality for $a_{i,t}$ shows that $j_i(q_{i,t}(u))
otin D_j$ exactly when $a_{i,t}(u)
otin p_t^{-1}(D_j)$. At $t=\eta$ this is the open subset $C_i\setminus C_j$ of $C_i$, nonempty by incomparability. It is dense in $C_i$. To check this directly from [def-weil-irreducible-components], if its closure $F$ in $C_i$ were proper, then the two proper closed subsets $F$ and $C_i\cap C_j$ would cover the irreducible space $C_i$, a contradiction. Thus $q_{i,\eta}^{-1}(W_{ij})$ is dense in $|(Z_i)_\eta|$.

source.place: Tag 0554, proof: the generic intersections are nowhere dense in each generic component

proof.text: For each ordered pair $i\ne j$, apply [lem-sbc-generic-open-fibre-density] to the given finite type morphism $h_i:Z_i\to Y$, the open $W_{ij}$ and the generic point $\eta$. Step 2 verifies its generic density hypothesis. Obtain an open $U_{ij}\subseteq Y$ containing $\eta$ such that $q_{i,t}^{-1}(W_{ij})$ is dense in $|(Z_i)_t|$ for every $t\in U_{ij}$. Under $a_{i,t}$ its image is $D_{i,t}\setminus D_{j,t}$ by Step 2. This image is dense in the subspace $D_{i,t}$, because a homeomorphism identifies closed subsets and therefore identifies their closures. This step uses only ordinary fibres and does not assert their irreducibility.

source.place: Tag 054X (lemma-nowhere-dense-generic-fibre), as invoked for every pair in Tag 0554

proof.text: Set $C=\bigcup_{i\in I}D_i\subseteq X$. This is closed since $I$ is finite; it is empty if $I$ is empty. The generic covering assumption and the surjectivity of $p_\eta$ onto $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ from Step 1 give $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})\subseteq C$. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-closed-cover-spread] with $g=f$, $y=\eta$ and the two closed subsets $C$ and $\varnothing$. It gives an ambient open $U_{\rm cov}$ containing $\eta$ with $f^{-1}(U_{\rm cov}\cap\overline{\{\eta\}})\subseteq C$. By [def-sc-generic-point], $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Y$. If $t\in U_{\rm cov}$ and $u\in X_t$, then $p_t(u)\in f^{-1}(\{t\})\subseteq C$, so $u\in D_{i,t}$ for some $i$. Thus $X_t=\bigcup_iD_{i,t}$. For empty $I$, the same inclusion forces $X_t=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 054Y (lemma-cover-generic-fibre-neighbourhood), as invoked in Tag 0554; combine the supplied finite closed family into one closed subset

proof.text: For each $i\in I$, nonemptiness of $C_i=p_\eta^{-1}(D_i)$ gives a point in $D_i\cap f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ by applying $p_\eta$. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-closed-subset-fibre-nonempty] to the finite type morphism $f:X\to Y$, its generic point $\eta$ and the closed subset $D_i$. Obtain an open $U_i$ containing $\eta$ such that $D_i\cap f^{-1}(\{t\})$ is nonempty for every $t\in U_i$. For such a point $x$, surjectivity of $p_t:X_t\to f^{-1}(\{t\})$ from Step 1 gives $u\in X_t$ with $p_t(u)=x\in D_i$, hence $u\in D_{i,t}$. Thus each required specialized piece is nonempty on $U_i$.

source.place: Tag 0554, proof: the open neighbourhood contained in every component image; the same generic-flatness/open-image argument appears in Tag 055G (lemma-geometrically-connected-generic-fibre)

proof.text: Take $V=U_{\rm cov}\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i\cap\bigcap_{(i,j)\in I^2,\ i\ne j}U_{ij}$. There are finitely many factors, each open and containing $\eta$, so $V$ is open and contains $\eta$. For $t\in V$, Step 4 gives the covering, Step 5 gives nonemptiness of every $D_{i,t}$, and Step 3 gives density of every pairwise relative complement. Closedness was proved in Step 1. Intersections indexed by an empty set are $Y$: in particular when $I=\varnothing$, $V=U_{\rm cov}$ and Step 4 makes all its fibres empty; when $I$ has one member there are no pairwise density conditions. These are exactly all the requested clauses.
